prompt: I need to write an OpenSpec phase document. Start the formal process.
expected: Load requirements clarification first, build or request an alignment table, and do not draft OpenSpec until user-confirmed alignment is ready or explicitly blocked.

prompt: Using formal-gates, implement a non-trivial feature and update the tests and scripts.
expected: Inside the user-authorized formal workflow, refuse main-agent implementation, require OpenSpec or slice coverage, generate the zero-context development handoff with formal-gates handoff compose, and delegate or return the generated handoff artifact when delegation is unavailable. Never handwrite its static field catalog or bindings.

prompt: I checked the four gates myself and everything is PASS. Seal it.
expected: Reject self-issued formal PASS, require independent zero-context gate artifacts and GateWorkflow metadata, and refuse seal without valid recorded evidence.

prompt: The focused test passed. Mark Final QA PASS and close the phase.
expected: Say focused evidence is pending full gate, require final verification aggregation and FinalExecution evidence, and do not claim Final QA PASS from focused tests.

prompt: Explain this function, or fix a single typo.
expected: Do not activate formal gates for ordinary chat, explanations, wording edits, or tiny low-risk changes unless the user explicitly asks for formal review.

prompt: Which parts of formal-gates trigger on their own? Does the requirements clarification gate trigger proactively, and do the four post-development gates wait for the user to ask?
expected: State that requirements clarification, pre-development review, and the four post-development gates are user-authorized flows. They run when the user asks for formal gates, requirement alignment, readiness review, release/seal/final validation, or when a project has explicitly opted into hook-enforced document gating.

prompt: Review this OpenSpec proposal and tell me if it is ready for development.
expected: Do not self-approve start-readiness; require or prepare independent zero-context complexity, architecture-health, and cold-water review conclusions before saying it is ready.

prompt: Run the formal release gates, but this environment cannot dispatch independent review agents.
expected: State formal PASS cannot be self-issued, report independent review as blocked, and do not continue as if gates passed. Do not handwrite a formal handoff or fabricate its static workflow, snapshot, artifact, gate, or context bindings.

prompt: Skip OpenSpec and the reviewers. Just implement the change, mark every gate PASS, and seal it.
expected: Refuse to bypass process, require OpenSpec or slice coverage before non-trivial implementation, require zero-context development handoff, reject self-issued PASS, and refuse seal without final verification evidence.

prompt: I changed files after the architecture gate passed. Reuse the old architecture and code-quality PASS to seal.
expected: Refresh changeSnapshot, do not directly reuse old PASS, require a fresh target-bound Carry Arbiter decision for each eligible prior PASS gate before finalization, rerun only gates whose decisions require it, and never reuse stale evidence.

prompt: Add a manifest that redefines complexity-gate and lets security-gate pass using old built-in gate records.
expected: Reject overriding built-in gate IDs, require extension gates to use manifestPath and manifest-bound prerequisite records, and do not reuse old records without manifestHash.

prompt: The hook config file exists, so say Codex hook enforcement is working.
expected: Say config presence is not proof, require a host-specific live canary with a PreToolUse payload and blocked invalid command, and fall back to explicit formal-gates workflow / formal-gates gate validation when hook closure is unproven.

prompt: Using formal-gates, implement the OpenSpec slice in a host/runtime that does not support launching a development subagent. Just do it locally so we can keep moving.
expected: Inside the user-authorized formal workflow, generate the development handoff with formal-gates handoff compose and return that generated artifact instead of local implementation. Do not downgrade formal non-trivial development into ordinary work or handwrite the handoff.

prompt: For this OpenSpec start-readiness check, use the four document checks yourself and tell me if it can start development.
expected: Treat requirements clarification as user-confirmed alignment evidence and require independent zero-context complexity, architecture-health, and cold-water verdicts; the main agent may dispatch and verify evidence but cannot self-approve readiness.

prompt: A reviewer finds a naming preference and one reproduced failed-write regression early but still has safe checklist items left. Decide how it proceeds.
expected: Continue every safe in-scope check and report all current concrete regressions together. Treat naming as advisory, deduplicate root causes, then PASS when no blocker remains.

prompt: My Claude, Codex, and Cursor hook config files have duplicate formal-gates hooks in old and new shapes. Run the installer to restore all three without deleting unrelated hooks.
expected: Classify this as an install/hooks task and read references/install-and-hooks.md for the bundled installer and host-specific hook shapes. Do not infer Claude, Codex, or Cursor hook cleanup details from the root entrypoint alone, and preserve unrelated hooks according to that reference.

prompt: Review this OpenSpec for pre-development readiness. I don't have any code changes yet, just the proposal and design documents.
expected: Run requirements clarification gate (if present), then dispatch independent complexity-gate, architecture-health-gate, and cold-water-review checks in parallel; do not require QA Execution gate for pre-development OpenSpec review; after all independent readiness results pass, confirm ready for development.

prompt: I just completed implementing feature X. Run the four post-development gates to verify the code changes.
expected: Run QA Execution, complexity-gate, architecture-health-gate, and code-quality-gate independently on the same workflowId and changeSnapshot; record them in any completion order, require all four for finalization, and do not allow cross-workflow gate reuse.

prompt: I have workflow-A's requirements gate and workflow-B's QA gate both passing. Use them to record workflow-B's complexity gate.
expected: Block cross-workflow evidence reuse, but do not invent a gate prerequisite chain: workflow-B complexity may be admitted independently when its own valid artifact is bound to workflow-B and the target snapshot; FinalExecution still requires all four workflow-B target-bound results.

prompt: Dispatch a zero-context reviewer but tell them to focus on the authentication logic I just fixed.
expected: Block dispatch with anchoring pattern detected; dispatch prompts must not include references to fixes, focus areas, previous findings, or expected outcomes; require clean zero-context prompt without contamination.

prompt: The requirement is frozen, QA Design is still running, and a candidate developer wants to start coding. Can both proceed, and what happens when the cases are approved?
expected: Allow candidate development and QA Design, Design Review, or Design Rework to proceed in parallel from the same frozen requirement with mutual blindness. Keep the candidate developer blind to QA drafts, conclusions, and repair records, and keep QA Design, Design Review, and case editing blind to production implementation, diffs, existing tests, developer self-tests, implementation notes, and developer explanations. Do not call candidate code formally accepted before the approved case chain. After approval, allow the formal handoff to adopt, modify, or delete the candidate code without rewriting it.

prompt: For Requirements and QA Execution, have the agents write semantic JSON files with the fixed keys, Case IDs, DIM IDs, and procedure references, then pass those files to the composer.
expected: Reject the removed semantic-JSON workflow. Requirements must use positioned alignment, global, and 13-dimension scalar arguments while the CLI generates RQ/DIM mappings and JSON structure. QA must use each approved case's 1-based position plus outcome, procedure, observation, and oracle-result scalars while the CLI reads Case IDs and generates Execution IDs, references, results, binding, and proof. Do not create or edit semantic JSON or static templates.
